transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-07-07
Start: 14:00 PDT
Duration: ~52 minutes
Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Arjun (Redwood SE), Lena (Peregrine - Head of ML), Tom (Peregrine - VP Product), Ravi (Peregrine - Infra)

Summary:
Quick operational runway / rightsize sync focused on cost tradeoffs for high-traffic retail inference (personalization & search rerank), feasibility of a short dedicated pilot, and next steps for load testing and security docs.

Topics:
- Current usage patterns and spike events
- Cost per 10k tokens vs dedicated pool economics
- Reliability and failover (Redwood Dedicate/Private options)
- Security: SOC2, SAML, KMS, audit logs
- Pilot scope + timeline

00:00 Maya (Redwood): Hey everyone, thanks for joining, appreciate you blocking time. we wanted to run through where you are with the rollout and try to line up a pilot that demonstrates the cost savings and stability.
00:35 Tom (Peregrine): Yeah thanks Maya, we got a lot riding on this for the fall promo window. main question for us is can we get consistent p95 under 300ms for short rerank calls, and still hit our cost targets.
01:10 Lena (Peregrine): Also from ML side we will be very sensitive to small regressions; we need model output parity and deterministic KV cache behavior.
01:38 Arjun (Redwood SE): Totally. quick TL;DR from infra: Dedicated pools give predictable throughput, and the runtime has KV cache and continuous batching. sometimes the transcripter writes "KV cash" — so ignore that. we can pin model versions and snapshot kvs for consistent behavior.
02:10 Ravi (Peregrine): When you say predictable throughput, what headroom do we get for 2x spikes? last holiday we saw a sustained 2.4x for ~3 hours.
02:38 Arjun: For dedicated we recommend a primary pool sized for 1.2-1.5x baseline with burst capacity for spikes. the burst can be turned on as a reserve or we can do autoscale but that affects the unit economics. if you enable autoscale you pay for shorter windows at on-demand rates.
03:05 Tom: That is the key tradeoff. finance is saying dedicated commit if we can show 30-40% per-token savings versus hosted.
03:25 Maya: Right. we'll run numbers after the loadbench but ballpark from similar retail workloads we've seen 28-37% savings with a 3-6 month reserved pool vs. pure hosted at p50 latencies
03:50 Lena: Any nuance with quantized models? we run a 7B-ish model with GPT-style attention; if you quantize to 4-bit do we risk output delta?
04:18 Arjun: Good question. we provide quantization profiles; for some workloads the quality delta is negligible, for others you may need mixed precision for critical rerank. we'll include model-specific delta metrics in the pilot. note the term "Redwood Dedicatedy" sometimes gets mangled in transcriptions.
04:45 Ravi: Security — we're required to have SAML SSO, customer-managed KMS, and audit logs forwarded to our SIEM. can Redwood handle that from a Dedicated or Private install?
05:12 Maya: Yes. Dedicated supports customer KMS integrations and audit logs; Private (VPC/on-prem) gives you even more control. we'll share the SOC 2 doc and the SAML integration guide.
05:38 Tom: Do you have examples of customers who used private for compliance?
05:50 Maya: We have several enterprise customers in regulated industries; we'll share redacted case notes.
06:10 Speaker 1 (automated): [inaudible] background noise.
06:30 Lena: Quick note — our key success criteria for the pilot: p95 ≤ 350ms end-to-end for rerank, less than 10% model quality drift on our evals, and total cost improvement ≥ 25% over current hosted vendor baseline.
07:05 Arjun: That's a clear bar. for the loadbench we'll need sample traffic distribution, typical seq lengths, and the percent of streaming vs non-streaming calls.
07:30 Lena: We'll provide a 48h sample of anonymized traces and the eval prompt set.
07:48 Ravi: What about failover? if a DC goes down, do you auto-route to another region and what are the cold-start effects?
08:10 Arjun: Smart routing can failover to a compatible model variant in another region. cold-starts are minimized by warm pools and prefix caching, but there is an unavoidable latency bump on a cross-region switchover. we can model that in the bench.
08:45 Tom: For finance, show us raw token cost and also token-equivalent inference cost when batching and kv cache hit rates are applied — we want to model real bill impact.
09:12 Maya: We'll deliver a cost workbook that models baseline hosted, dedicated reserved, and dedicated with burst. it will have sensitivity to cache hit rate and batch size.
09:35 Lena: Any limitations on batching due to our real-time SLAs? some rerank calls are sub-200ms budget, can't batch too long.
10:00 Arjun: Right — continuous batching adapts to latency SLOs; you can cap batching to meet p50 SLAs and still get some batching benefits. we'll show historic latency vs batch size tradeoffs.
10:30 Tom: On instrumentation, can we get token-level cost by route? that's important for product steering which features to throttle.
10:45 Maya: Yes, Redwood Console exposes per-route token breakdown plus traces and model rollouts. we'll grant you a demo workspace for the pilot.
11:05 Ravi: Network egress — our cloud bill will care if traffic crosses regions. can we pin workloads to a single region?
11:25 Arjun: Absolutely. routing policy can pin requests to region or fallback to nearest. Dedicated pools are typically regional. Private on-prem is of course fully local.
11:50 Lena: For the model itself, will you host our custom fine-tuned artifact or do we bring a container?
12:10 Arjun: We can ingest your model artifact and host it — we manage quantization and kernel selection. for Private deployments you can also run the runtime in your infra with our control plane.
12:38 Tom: We've heard from other vendors that their runtime is slow on KV caching at scale; can you describe how Redwood handles KV cache for multi-tenant workloads?
13:05 Arjun: The runtime segregates KV caches per customer and uses hot-key replication for sharded queries; we also support prefix/KV caching at the model router, which reduces recompute. note that under high churn warmup can still cost tokens until cache warms.
13:40 Lena: Okay, so for our pilot we'll want a cold-to-warm regime test as part of the loadbench.
13:55 Maya: makes sense.
14:05 Tom: Timeline — if we start loadbench 07/13 and run for 24-48h, when could we have a pilot pricing decision?
14:30 Maya: if loadbench is 07/13-07/14, Arjun runs analysis for 2 business days, we can get pricing proposal and SLA terms by 07/19.
14:50 Ravi: Are there minimums for a dedicated pool? like one whole GPU cluster or can we do fractional?
15:12 Arjun: Dedicated is reserved capacity, typically a pool of GPUs; we price by vGPU equivalent. you don't need a whole cluster but commitments are by capacity units. we'll include a sample sizing and lease term options in the workbook.
15:40 Tom: For the holiday window we may want burst to public hosted for extra headroom for a week; is that supported?
16:05 Maya: yes, that's exactly the burst scenario we recommend — keep baseline on dedicated and configure a burst policy to hosted or extra dedicated warm nodes.
16:30 Lena: On the quality guardrails: do you provide eval monitoring and automatic rollback if generation quality regresses?
16:50 Arjun: Redwood Optimize monitors prompt/eval sets and can trigger regressions and rollbacks or canary routes. we'll include a sample alerting workflow.
17:15 Speaker 2 (background): [crosstalk]
17:30 Tom: Procurement question — what's your standard term for a pilot? finance asks about liability and data handling.
17:48 Maya: For pilots we do a time-limited contract with data use limited to the pilot scope, plus an interim NDA if needed. we'll share a pilot MSA template.
18:10 Ravi: Can audit logs be exported to our SIEM in near real-time? we prefer syslog or cloudwatch?
18:30 Arjun: We support forwarding logs to your SIEM via secure forwarders; formats include JSON over TLS; we'll include a sample configuration.
18:58 Lena: One logistic — for the loadbench Arjun will need an API key; can we use a dev key scoped to test routes?
19:20 Maya: Yes, we'll issue scoped keys for the bench, and rotate them afterwards.
19:40 Tom: Can you show us a quick sketch of the cost workbook variables? I'm mostly curious about cache hit rate sensitivity and burst pricing.
20:05 Maya: Sure. (screen share cue) the workbook will have baseline qps, average seq length, cache hit rate, batch size, reserved capacity cost, burst per-token multiplier, and estimated monthly spend.
20:40 Arjun: For numbers, historically with retail rerank at 7B models we often see cache hit rates 30-65% depending on prefix reuse; that dramatically changes per-token costs.
21:05 Ravi: Any telemetry overhead on our side for tracing? we need to add trace headers but minimal changes to our gateway.
21:25 Arjun: Just propagate trace headers and user id; Redwood Console captures route traces with minimal instrumentation. we'll send integration notes.
21:45 Lena: Regarding model parity checks, do you run diff tests or roundtrip evals?
22:05 Arjun: We run both — token-level diffs, n-gram overlap and your eval prompt set to compute delta. we also do human-in-the-loop checks if needed.
22:30 Tom: How do you handle model rollouts — can we do canary 5% then 25%?
22:50 Arjun: Yes, rollouts and A/B are supported, plus automatic fallback if errors exceed thresholds.
23:12 Speaker 1: [small audio hiccup]
23:30 Maya: quick recap: we need sample traces, sample evals, approval to run loadbench 07/13, and confirmation on who signs pilot MSA.
23:50 Lena: I'll be owner for evals and traces. procurement will loop in legal for the MSA.
24:10 Tom: Finance will review pricing once you send workbook.
24:30 Ravi: I'll coordinate infra endpoints and SIEM integration.
25:00 Arjun: I'll prepare the bench steps and a script to replay traces with concurrency patterns; also will collect p50/p95 token costs and tail latencies.
25:35 Maya: Great. any other risks we should call out?
25:48 Lena: Model drift during quantization is the main one.
26:05 Arjun: We'll surface quality delta metrics and recommend mixed-precision if drift is > X%.
26:28 Tom: Another risk is unanticipated egress charges if routing cross-region during spikes.
26:45 Maya: we'll add egress sensitivity to the workbook.
27:05 Speaker 3 (unknown): [laughs softly]
27:20 Lena: For the pilot scope, can we limit the test routes to search rerank first, then expand to personalization?
27:40 Maya: yes, recommended to start with the high-volume, lower-latency route like rerank to validate economics.
27:58 Tom: Ok, what's the decision gate after bench — do we need exec sign-off?
28:15 Lena: If pilot shows >=25% cost improvement and p95 within 350ms, we'll recommend a go-ahead to exec.
28:35 Maya: noted.
28:50 Arjun: Logistics for bench: I'll need access to anonymized traces (S3 link), a test API key, and expected QPS profile. after the bench I will run the analysis and attach a report.
29:15 Ravi: We'll prepare S3 and a temporary IAM role for Redwood.
29:38 Maya: I'll follow up with the MSA template and SOC2.
29:55 Tom: For billing, if we go dedicated afterwards do you invoice monthly or quarterly?
30:10 Maya: Options exist for monthly or annual commitments; commitments yield stronger discounts. we'll lay out terms.
30:30 Lena: For the quality gates, besides p95 and cost, can we require zero regression on top-10 rerank precision?
30:50 Arjun: we can include that metric in the eval pass/fail criteria.
31:05 Speaker 2: [paper rustling]
31:20 Tom: One technical detail—our product uses 128-token average sequence for rerank, but we sometimes request 512 tokens for long context. is the kernel selection adaptive?
31:45 Arjun: Yes, kernel selection and compilation picks paths optimized for seq length. long sequences increase per-token cost, but the runtime can pipeline and use kv cache to mitigate.
32:05 Ravi: Will the loadbench simulate mixed-seq lengths? we want realistic distribution.
32:20 Arjun: yes, we'll replay the distribution you give us.
32:40 Lena: Does the console provide anomaly alerts? like sudden drop in cache hit rate or spike in latencies?
32:55 Maya: yes, Redwood Console can alert on these signals and create a ticket or webhook to your pager.
33:20 Tom: Are there any known degradations with canary rollbacks when using caching? could the cache cause inconsistent rollbacks?
33:40 Arjun: Cache keys are tied to model variant; rollbacks can invalidate caches, but we have mechanisms to gracefully warm new caches. we'll show that in the bench report.
34:05 Speaker 1: [phone vibrating]
34:22 Maya: okay timeline recap: loadbench 07/13-07/14, analysis by 07/15-07/16, pricing + SLA 07/19. any objections?
34:45 Lena: none from ML.
34:55 Tom: finance ok with that.
35:12 Ravi: infra ok.
35:30 Maya: Great. quick Q — do you want Redwood to include a short failover simulation (region down)?
35:50 Lena: yes, please include that.
36:05 Arjun: will do.
36:20 Tom: For the pilot MSA, who at Redwood signs?
36:40 Maya: I'll be your AE point and legal will provide a pilot addendum; I'll share contact.
36:58 Speaker 2: [soft cough]
37:12 Lena: Any competitive considerations we should know? some of our peers tested Anthropic and Vertex; cost was higher on Anthropic and Vertex had variance in quantization.
37:40 Maya: Understood. we'll include competitor baseline in the workbook where possible.
37:58 Arjun: we can also run a side-by-side but that costs extra; we can discuss if you want that as part of the pilot.
38:20 Tom: Maybe later. for now, focus on Redwood numbers.
38:40 Maya: Understood. action owners recap in chat.
38:55 Arjun: I'll share the bench playbook and a small runbook for SIEM forwarding.
39:10 Lena: We'll get the sample traces uploaded by 07/10.
39:30 Ravi: I'll set up the temporary IAM and an S3 path.
39:50 Maya: I'll send calendar invites for the bench kickoff and follow-up review.
40:05 Tom: Anything else on costs — hidden fees, egress?
40:22 Maya: no hidden fees; egress is passed through at cost and we'll list assumptions.
40:40 Lena: Great.
40:55 Arjun: small tech note — quantization often reduces GPU memory and improves throughput, but sometimes increases latency variance; we'll measure both.
41:20 Tom: ok. if the bench shows we're close but not quite at 25% improvement, is there a fast follow-up? like short-term tuning?
41:40 Arjun: yes, we can tune batching, cache policy, and quant profiles; often you get incremental gains without more infrastructure.
42:05 Speaker 1: [muted]
42:20 Maya: any legal asks?
42:35 Tom: legal will review MSA; nothing blocking on our side for pilot.
42:50 Lena: one more — can you provide recent incident history and MTTR numbers for dedicated pools?
43:10 Maya: yes, we'll send a recent SLA report and MTTR averages.
43:30 Ravi: do you publish runbooks? we'd like to see failover runbook for region outage.
43:50 Arjun: we'll include a condensed runbook as part of the pilot materials.
44:10 Tom: timeline sounds good.
44:25 Maya: OK let's close with explicit next steps (I'll also paste in the email).
44:38 Maya (recap): 1) Arjun to run loadbench 07/13 with S3 traces (Owner: Arjun). 2) Peregrine to upload traces and sample evals by 07/10 (Owner: Lena). 3) Maya to send pilot pricing, SOC2, MSA template and scoped API keys by 07/09 (Owner: Maya). 4) Ravi to provision temporary IAM for S3 and SIEM forwarding test (Owner: Ravi).
45:20 Tom: sounds good.
45:35 Lena: we'll get started on traces.
45:50 Arjun: I'll prep the bench script and share it ahead of 07/13.
46:05 Maya: Any final questions?
46:20 Tom: none here. thanks.
46:35 Lena: thanks everyone.
46:50 Ravi: thanks.
47:05 Maya: I'll follow up with the email and calendar invites.
47:20 Speaker 1: [call ended tone]

Post-meeting notes:
- Pilot scope agreed: search rerank route first, dedicated pool baseline + burst to hosted for promo window; loadbench scheduled 07/13.
- Documents to send: SOC2 summary, SAML guide, KMS notes, MSA pilot template, sample cost workbook.
- Risk list: quantization drift, cross-region egress, cache warmup tail costs.
